name: Approach of the Second Sun
oracle_text: If this spell was cast from your hand and you've cast another spell named Approach of the Second Sun this game, you win the game. Otherwise, put Approach of the Second Sun into its owner's library seventh from the top and you gain 7 life.
blocked_sentences: If this spell was cast from your hand and you've cast another spell named Approach of the Second Sun this game, you win the game.
Otherwise, put Approach of the Second Sun into its owner's library seventh from the top and you gain 7 life.

needs.what: an `if` condition leaf that asks whether the spell being resolved was cast from its controller's hand -- `{"cast_from_hand": true}`, read off the resolving spell the way `cast_from_graveyard` is, so a spell can branch on the zone it was cast from
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `condition_keys` has `cast_from_graveyard`, which reads only the graveyard stamp, and its negation is not 'from hand' (a spell cast from exile, the command zone or the top of the library is neither). `zone_is` reports the source's CURRENT zone (engine/effects/conditions.py:156, and its own comment at :216 says it cannot answer where a spell was cast from), and a resolving spell is always on the stack. The engine already stamps the fact -- `obj.cast_from_hand` is set in engine/stack.py:78 and read by rebound and plot at :903 and :912 -- it is simply not exposed to the condition language, so this is a one-leaf change.

needs.what: a game-long ledger of the spells each player has cast, filterable by name, so 'you've cast another spell named Approach of the Second Sun this game' is a value leaf -- e.g. `{"spells_cast_this_game": {"player": "you", "filter": {"name": "Approach of the Second Sun"}}}` compared `>` against `{"const": 0}`, counting casts that happened on earlier turns and excluding this spell itself ('another')
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `spells_cast_this_turn` (value_keys) is the only cast counter and it lives on `TurnLedger` (engine/structs.py:1123, 1137), which is cleared at every turn boundary by `TurnLedger` reset at :1298-1299 -- so on the turn that matters it reads 0 and the card would never win. Nothing else records cast history: `set_flag` writes only to permanents on the battlefield (engine/effects/ops_combat_flags.py:107-110) and object flags do not survive a zone change, `set_turn_flag` is explicitly the one-turn lifetime, and there is no player-level, game-long record of any kind (the only game-long player fields are `epic_source` and the city's blessing).

needs.what: a card-level rider, beside `exiles_itself`, that sends the spell into its OWNER's library at a printed depth instead of the graveyard as it resolves -- e.g. `"tucks_itself": {"from_top": 7}` -- and, for this card, one that applies only on the 'Otherwise' branch
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `put_on_top` already understands the depth (`from_top: 7`, engine/effects/ops_cards.py:1880), but it cannot reach the resolving spell: `_place_after_resolution` runs AFTER `spell_effects` and moves a nonpermanent to the graveyard unconditionally (engine/stack.py:838-848), so a self-tuck written in the card's own effects is overwritten -- exactly the reason `exiles_itself` exists as a rider rather than an `exile` op, per the comment at engine/stack.py:889-893. Of the seven riders on that slot (`graveyard_cast_exiles`, buyback, rebound, cipher, `exiles_itself`, plot, adventure/aftermath) every one redirects to exile or to hand; none names a library, and none carries a depth.
